mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as seen in historical easing cycles.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 8.0% signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 8.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages indicates robust consumer demand that boosts corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed 12-month moving averages (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production declining below 95.0 (relative to 2017 base) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days during recessionary supply conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI increase above 2.5% signals inflationary pressure that triggers monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as the Fed raises rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 2.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment growth above 0.5% month-over-month indicates labor market strength that increases consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth exceeding 1.0% signals robust economic expansion that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days during strong growth regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 QoQ growth > 1.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 98.0 (relative to 2017 base) indicates manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 98.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
